artifact_role: digitization protocol for the official Berut 2012 Figure 3 raster candidates

preferred_first_candidate.rationale: Use the smaller large raster candidate first because it is likely a cropped or alternate panel that may be easier to calibrate. This is a workflow selection, not evidence that the candidate already contains a calibrated numeric row.

fallback_candidate.rationale: Retain the largest raster as fallback if jpeg_3 cannot be calibrated or does not expose the needed axes/curve clearly.

required_calibration_landmarks.purpose: Identify the rectangular plotting area before reading any curve or point.
Map horizontal pixel position into the source figure axis convention.
Map vertical pixel position into work/heat or normalized quantity before any numeric comparison to the topic summary row.
Anchor any extracted Berut curve/point to the Landauer-limit reference visible in the figure.
State exactly which visual element supports the topic summary row before transcription.

forbidden_until_complete: replacing the current topic-summary value with a digitized value
claiming external validation beyond lower-bound consistency

minimum_review_before_accepting_digits: candidate raster selected and archived by hash in the artifact
axis calibration values recorded in machine-readable form
digitized point or curve value reproducible from recorded pixel coordinates
claim wording remains summary-layer until mapping is reviewed

blocker_transition.why_narrower: The protocol now selects a first calibration candidate and defines the exact landmark fields required before numeric transcription. Remaining work is landmark coordinate capture, not deciding how to structure the digitization pass.

claim_boundary: This protocol narrows the Berut digitization workflow. It does not calibrate axes, select a real data point, transcribe a numeric value, or close source-normalized Berut evidence.
